summary:
[  edit  ]
The Trail  CHOP  displays a history of its input channels back in time. A window of time is displayed from the current frame back in time, the size of this window is set by the  Window  Length parameter. The last sample in the Trail  CHOP  is a sample of the input at the current frame.
Note:  If the input channels change in number or names, the Trail  CHOP  clears its trails and begins anew.  You can use a  Replace CHOP  in this case to create stand in values.

parameters.label: Active
parameters.name: active
parameters.description: When On the Trail  CHOP  will record its input.

parameters.label: Grow Length
parameters.name: growlength
parameters.description: When On the length of the Trail  CHOP 's recording will keep getting longer as the timeline moves forward. Use this for recording any length as needed.

parameters.label: Window  Length
parameters.name: wlength
parameters.description: The amount of history recorded is set by  Window  Length. The Units menu on the right determine which units to use in the parameter (Samples, Frames, Seconds). A setting of 4 seconds will show the value of the input channel for the previous 4 seconds.

parameters.label: Window  Length Unit
parameters.name: wlengthunit
parameters.description: Choose between using Samples, Frames, or Seconds as the units for the  Window  Length parameter.

parameters.label: Capture
parameters.name: capture
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines when to capture values.

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Captures a sliding window of the input every cook. Useful for capturing a continuous log.

parameters.label: Only When Input Cooks
parameters.name: inputcooks
parameters.description: Captures the input only whenever the input cooks. Useful for capturing discrete events separated by long pauses.

parameters.label: Resample
parameters.name: resample
parameters.description: Enable parameter below to resample the output to a different length.

parameters.label: Resample
parameters.name: samples
parameters.description: Resample the output to this specified length.

parameters.label: Rate
parameters.name: setrate
parameters.description: Enable parameter below to use a different sample rate.

parameters.label: Sample Rate
parameters.name: rate
parameters.description: Resample using this sample rate instead of the global frame rate ( $ FPS  ).

parameters.label: Reset
parameters.name: reset
parameters.description: While On, this toggle resets the channel(s) to 0.

parameters.label: Reset  Pulse
parameters.name: resetpulse
parameters.description: Click to instantly resets the channel(s) to 0.

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page. See  Pattern Matching .

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate
parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Use rate of first input to resample others.

parameters.label: Resample At Maximum Rate
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Resample to the highest sample rate.

parameters.label: Resample At Minimum Rate
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Resample to the lowest sample rate.

parameters.label: Error If Rates Differ
parameters.name: err
parameters.description: Doesn't accept conflicting sample rates.

parameters.label: Export  Method
parameters.name: exportmethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - This will determine how to connect the  CHOP  channel to the parameter. Refer to the  Export  article for more information.

parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the index of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Name

parameters.label: To "pulse" a parameter is to send it a signal from (1) an  exported  CHOP channel or (2) a python command or (3) a mouse click that causes a new action to occur immediately. A pulse via python is via the  .pulse()  function on a pulse
parameters.description: type parameter, such as Reset parameter in a  Speed CHOP . A pulse from a CHOP is typically a 0 to 1 to 0 signal in an exported channel.
